title: Reductivity of a smooth connected subdirect product
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Reductive means smooth and connected with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means that geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Split maximal tori, character lattices, roots, coroots, positive systems and simple-root bases are as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $G_1,G_0$ be reductive. Let $H\hookrightarrow G_1\times_F G_0$ be a smooth connected closed subgroup such that both coordinate projections $H\to G_i$ are surjective on underlying spaces. Then $H$ is reductive. No finiteness, separability or centrality of either projection kernel is assumed.

source.place: Assertion 23.20 and its proof, printed p.491: images of the unipotent radical under the two surjective projections are smooth connected unipotent normal subgroups.

proof.text: Write $p_i:H\to G_i$ for the two projection homomorphisms, $i\in\{1,0\}$. Each $G_i$ is smooth by the definition of reductive in the statement. Apply [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] to $G_i\to\operatorname{Spec}F$: its unique fibre is $G_i$, which is therefore reduced. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme], $A_i=F[G_i]$ has no nonzero nilpotents.

source.place: Assertion 23.20, printed p.491; smooth targets are reduced by Stacks Tag 056T (varieties-lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal).

proof.text: For either $i$, factor $p_i=j_i u_i$ by [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image], with $u_i:H\to D_i$ faithfully flat and $j_i:D_i\hookrightarrow G_i$ a closed immersion. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $D_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i/J_i)$ over $G_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. Surjectivity of $p_i$ on spaces implies surjectivity of $j_i$, so every prime of $A_i$ contains $J_i$. The intersection formula in [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] gives $J_i\subseteq\sqrt{(0)}=0$, by step 1. Thus $j_i$ is an isomorphism, and $p_i$ is faithfully flat: its coordinate-algebra map is the faithfully flat map for $u_i$ after identifying $F[D_i]$ with $A_i$. This uses no smoothness of a projection kernel.

source.place: Assertion 23.20, printed p.491, interpreting surjective projections via Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; Stacks Tag 00E0 (algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology), part (7).

proof.text: Let $N\subseteq H$ be any smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to $p_i|_N$ to obtain homomorphisms $q_i:N\to I_i$ and $k_i:I_i\hookrightarrow G_i$, with $q_i$ faithfully flat, $k_i$ a closed immersion, and $p_i|_N=k_i q_i$. All groups here are affine and of finite type as required. Apply [lem-sfb-unipotent-normal-quotient-image] with $A=H$, $D=G_i$, $f=p_i$, $u=q_i$ and $j=k_i$. The ambient map is faithfully flat by step 2, and $N$ has exactly the required smoothness, connectedness, normality and geometric-point unipotence. It follows that $I_i$ is smooth, connected and unipotent and $k_i(I_i)$ is normal in $G_i$.

source.place: Assertion 23.20 and its proof, printed p.491

proof.text: Reductivity of $G_i$, as defined in the statement, now forces the closed subgroup scheme $k_i(I_i)$ to be the identity subgroup. Consequently $p_i|_N$ is the trivial homomorphism for both $i=1,0$. For any commutative $F$-algebra $R$ and $n\in N(R)$, its image in $G_1(R)\times G_0(R)$ is therefore $(1,1)$. The inclusion of $N$ in $H$ and that of $H$ in the product are injective on $R$-points by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Comparing $n$ with the identity shows $N(R)=\{1\}$ for every $R$, including nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Assertion 23.20 and its proof, printed p.491

proof.text: To make the last conclusion scheme-theoretic without a point-density argument, put $C=F[N]$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the universal point of $N(C)$ corresponds to $\operatorname{id}_C:C\to C$, whereas its identity point corresponds to $C\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}F\xrightarrow{\eta}C$, with $\varepsilon$ the identity-section map. Step 4 gives $\operatorname{id}_C=\eta\varepsilon$. Since $\varepsilon\eta=\operatorname{id}_F$, the structure map $\eta$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\varepsilon$. Hence $N$ is the trivial group scheme. Every smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup of $H$ is thus trivial. The assumed smoothness and connectedness of $H$ prove its reductivity.

source.place: Assertion 23.20 and its proof, printed p.491

proof_origin.place: Assertion 23.20 and its proof, printed p.491; Theorem 3.34, printed p.75. The radical argument is applied to an arbitrary smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, so no existence theorem for the unipotent radical is needed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q82-28505af55 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, every cited statement, and Milne iAG2017 23.19–23.20 (printed p.491). The item restates Milne 23.20 for an arbitrary smooth connected closed H in G1×G0 whose projections are surjective on spaces. It runs the argument on any smooth connected normal unipotent N, so no radical-existence theorem is needed, and the statement is true. Edge cases checked: trivial factors, products, the diagonal, isogeny and Frobenius graphs with infinitesimal kernels, and the excluded non-surjective cases B⊂SL2 and the trivial-homomorphism graph. Step 1: smooth implies geometrically reduced (tool use declared and accepted as generic), so A_i is reduced. Step 2: flat-image factorization; surjectivity on spaces puts J_i in every prime, the radical leaf gives J_i ⊆ √0 = 0, so p_i is faithfully flat. Step 3: all hypotheses of unipotent-normal-quotient-image are met. Steps 4–5: R-point injectivity and Yoneda give N trivial. No new nodes, no cycle, no duplicate found by DAG search, no SGA, and the citer compatible-rank-one-graph step 3 matches the hypotheses. Batch-5: the flagged lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection is the generic Mathlib leaf Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap. It is not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so it is accepted.

reviewed_lean.note: Every clause matches the node and Milne 23.20 (p.491). F: Field + IsAlgClosed. G1, G0: ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsReductive, which tests after AlgebraicClosure F and equals the node's convention because F is algebraically closed. H: affine, LFT+QC, Smooth, ConnectedSpace, nothing more. i : H ⟶ G1 ⊗ G0 with IsClosedSubgroupScheme, the product being the fibre product over F. Surjective on underlying spaces for i≫fst (G1) and i≫snd (G0). No kernel condition. Conclusion IsReductive H, same predicate, not weakened. Edge cases: trivial factors, product, diagonal, Frobenius graph with nonsmooth kernel, every characteristic; B⊂SL2 excluded only by surjectivity, as in the source. Single universe u, no unbound variables. Item changes only in lean, all dependency node files byte-identical to live, statement verbatim, no definitions, proof sorry, docstrings carry source place, blueprint tag and all 5 steps, report has both sections.
